x: Hoath moved up on this lap to take Bingham's place in 6th position (37mins. 46secs.), while the Finchley man lost 7th place to Ferguson, of Birchfield, with Holden behind Bingham in 9th place.

Bill was striding comfortably down the home straight in third place when Ferguson, of Highgate, came with a late burst to beat him by inches and so another chance of being the second Englishman home was lost.
After a very fast start the runners soon settled down to a more sociable pace and at the end of two miles Ferguson, of Highgate, Field, T.V.H., and Thompson, of Shaftesbury, were leading.
Ted Smith had an off day, but Eglington and Ferguson showed improved form. Charlie Speechley, our evergreen at sixty-five years of age, again showed he can still show the youngsters how.
At the start Dennis Merrett went away well, held his own and indeed gained a trifle to hand over to Ron Holtum who, although he had a bad cold, ran well to catch Ferguson of Notts.
